mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares bulk stress with longitudinal and tangential stresses in a solid?

options.A: Bulk stress acts uniformly in all directions, while longitudinal stress acts only along the axis of the applied force.
options.B: Bulk stress acts only on surfaces parallel to the applied force, whereas tangential stress acts perpendicular to those surfaces.
options.C: Longitudinal stress and bulk stress are identical, but tangential stress is half their magnitude.
options.D: Bulk stress varies with the shape of the object, while longitudinal and tangential stresses are independent of geometry.

mcqs.answer: Bulk stress acts uniformly in all directions, while longitudinal stress acts only along the axis of the applied force.
mcqs.explanation: Bulk (hydrostatic) stress is a normal stress that is equal in magnitude on all faces of an element and acts equally in every direction. Longitudinal stress is a normal stress that acts only along the length of the material where the force is applied. Tangential (shear) stress acts parallel to the surface. Therefore option A correctly captures the comparison.

mcqs.question: In a solid circular shaft of radius r subjected to a torque T, the tangential (shear) stress τ at the outer surface is given by:
mcqs.explanation: For a solid circular shaft, the polar moment of inertia J = π r⁴/2. The shear stress due to torque is τ = T r / J = T r / (π r⁴/2) = 2T/(π r³). Option B matches this expression. Option C is another form of the same formula but uses diameter d; substituting d = 2r gives τ = 2T/(π r³), which is equivalent, but the option as written includes the extra factor 16, making it incorrect as presented. Options A and D are missing the factor 2.

mcqs.question: Stress in a material is defined as:
mcqs.explanation: Stress is the internal restoring force that develops within a material when external forces are applied, expressed as force divided by the area over which it acts (σ = F/A). The other options describe different physical quantities: force per unit volume is pressure gradient, displacement per unit length is strain, and energy per unit mass is specific energy.

mcqs.question: A metal rod of cross‑sectional area 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ m² is subjected to a tensile force of 500 N. What is the normal stress in the rod?
mcqs.explanation: Stress σ = F/A = 500 N / (2.0 × 10⁻⁴ m²) = 2.5 × 10⁶ Pa. Option B is the correct calculation. The other options result from misplaced decimal places or incorrect division.

mcqs.question: Longitudinal stress in a rod differs from bulk stress in that:

options.A: Longitudinal stress acts perpendicular to the surface, while bulk stress acts parallel.
options.B: Longitudinal stress is caused by forces applied along the length, whereas bulk stress is hydrostatic and acts equally in all directions.
options.C: Longitudinal stress varies with temperature, bulk stress does not.
options.D: Longitudinal stress is always compressive, bulk stress is always tensile.

mcqs.answer: Longitudinal stress is caused by forces applied along the length, whereas bulk stress is hydrostatic and acts equally in all directions.
mcqs.explanation: Longitudinal (normal) stress arises when a force is applied along the axis of a member, producing tension or compression along that direction. Bulk (hydrostatic) stress is a uniform pressure that acts equally in every direction, such as the pressure experienced by a fluid or a solid submerged deep underwater. Options A, C, and D misstate the nature of these stresses.

mcqs.question: A submarine at a depth where the water exerts a pressure of 5 × 10⁶ Pa experiences bulk stress in its hull. Which statement best describes this stress?

options.A: It acts only on the top surface of the hull.
options.B: It acts uniformly in all directions on every element of the hull.
options.C: It acts only tangentially along the hull surface.
options.D: It varies linearly from top to bottom of the hull.

mcqs.answer: It acts uniformly in all directions on every element of the hull.
mcqs.explanation: Bulk (hydrostatic) stress is the same in magnitude and direction at a point, acting equally on all faces of an infinitesimal element. In a submerged object, the external water pressure produces this uniform stress throughout the material of the hull. Options A, C, and D incorrectly describe the distribution of hydrostatic pressure.

mcqs.question: A rectangular beam of width 0.05 m and height 0.10 m is subjected to a transverse shear force of 2000 N. Where does the maximum tangential (shear) stress occur in the cross‑section?
mcqs.explanation: For a rectangular cross‑section under shear, the shear stress distribution is parabolic, reaching its maximum at the neutral axis (the centroid) and dropping to zero at the outer surfaces. Hence option A is correct. Options B and C describe locations of minimum shear stress, and D is incorrect because the stress is not uniform.

mcqs.question: A concrete column of cross‑section 0.2 m² supports a vertical load of 400 kN. According to the definition of stress, what is the stress experienced by the column?
mcqs.explanation: Stress σ = Force/Area. Convert 400 kN to newtons: 400 kN = 400,000 N. σ = 400,000 N / 0.2 m² = 2,000,000 N/m² = 2 MPa. Option B matches this value. Options A, C, and D result from incorrect unit conversion or arithmetic errors.
